THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 15TH SEPTEMBER, 2023 AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT, THIS DAY, UMESH M ADIGA J.,
DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This is claimant's appeal against the judgment and award dated 27.08.2020 passed in M.V.C.No.491 of 2019 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, SIRA (for short, hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') for enhancement of compensation.
2. The matter is slated for hearing on admission and with the consent of the learned advocates on both the sides, the matter is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, we refer to the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal.
4. It is the case of appellant/claimant that on 06.03.2019, he was going by walk at the side of the road, near Vaddanahalli Village.
He met with an accident by the Maruti Omini Car bearing Registration number KA-01-MC- NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB 3019, due to rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver.
As a result of the same, claimant had sustained grievous injuries to the spinal cord.

Initially, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Sira and as per medical advice, he was admitted in Hemavathi Hospital,
Tumakuru, where in he underwent surgeries.
He had spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses.
5. Claimant has further contended that he was aged about 50 years at the time of accident.
He was coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He sustained fracture of T11 to L1 of vertebra with paraplegia; he is bed ridden.

His wife as well as two attendants around the clock have been Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
2 attending him;
He has been paying wages to attendant.
He has been wheelchair bound and has been suffering from disability to an extent of 100% to the whole body.
He is unable to do any work and lost his earnings.
Even after the treatment, he could not recover.
With NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB these reasons, he prayed to award compensation of Rs.50 lakhs.
6. Both the respondents, i.e., owner and insurer of the offended car had denied the contention of the claimant.
They had contended that accident had taken place due to negligence of the claimant; that the said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2 and it is liable to pay compensation.
7. Respondent No.2 had contended that owner of the Car had violated terms and conditions of policy of insurance.
Therefore, it was not liable to indemnify Respondent No.1.
It also denied contents of claim petition.
With these reasons, both the respondents have prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
8. The Tribunal had framed necessary issues for consideration.
Claimant had examined PWs-1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P30.
The Respondents had not lead oral or documentary evidence.
10. The Tribunal, after hearing both the parties and on appreciating pleadings and evidence on record, held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.

The Tribunal assessed age of claimant as 40 years, his income as Rs.14,000/- per month; permanent disability to an extent of 100%; and applied multiplier as '13' and awarded following amount of compensation:

Loss of amenities & enjoyment 50,000  of life  NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
3  8. Towards future medical 50,000  expenses  Total 26,45,904  11.
Accordingly, the Tribunal disposed of M.V.C.No.491 of 2019 by impugned judgment and award dated 27.08.2020.
The same has been challenged by claimant in this appeal on the ground of inadequate compensation.

12. We have heard the arguments of learned Advocate for the appellant and Respondent No.2.
13.
The learned Advocate for appellant has submitted that the Tribunal has not considered the income of the claimant properly.
The Tribunal has also not awarded just and reasonable amount of compensation on all the heads.
The Tribunal has not added future prospects to the income of claimant, who is aged about 50 years and has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100%.
Hence 25 to 30% of his income has to NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB be added to his income and compensation needs to be re- calculated.
Hence prayed to enhance the same.
14. The learned Advocate for Respondent No.2/ Insurer has submitted that, income of claimant assessed by the Tribunal is on higher side.
It is settled law that the income of claimant has to be assessed on the basis of Minimum Wages Act and not on the basis of notional income considered while settlement of the dispute in Lok- Adalath.
He has further submitted that, even if this court intend to consider future prospects, it cannot be more than 10% because the claimant was aged about 50 years at a time of accident.

As per the law laid down in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1 between the age group of 50 to 60, the future prospects could be taken at the rate of 10% and hence, the said percentage is not between 25 to 30% as contended by the appellant.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that, the compensation awarded (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB under other heads are just and reasonable and there is no need for interference by this Court and prays to dismiss the appeal.
15. The learned Advocates for both the parties facilitated some reliances.
16. From the rival contentions of the parties, the following questions arise for our determination.
"Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"

Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
4 17.
The manner in which the accident had taken place is not in serious dispute.
The Tribunal, after appreciating the evidence on record, has held that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
The said finding is not challenged by Respondents.

Therefore,
there is no need to reconsider the same.
18. It is not in dispute that claimant is an agricultural coolie.

Tribunal assessed his income as NC:
2023:KHC:41715-DB Rs.14,000/- per month, on the basis of chart of notional wages table prepared by KSLSA.
The Central Government issued Notification under the provisions of Minimum wages Act, fixing Guidelines to pay Minimum Wages to different class of labourers.

As per said pertaining to payment of compensations to victim of an accident is notification, minimum wages of an agricultural coolie is Rs.401/- i.e., Rs.12,000/- per month and about Rs.2000/- less than the notional income fixed by KSLSA, relating to present case.
19. Provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, benevolent legislation.
The Act does not give any Table of notional income to assess income of a victim of an accident.
Hence, income shall be assessed on the basis of facts and circumstances in each case.

20. Normally, wages of unorganised labour in a particular area depends upon various factors, such as, demand and supply of labours, standard of living, literacy of the people and in case of agriculture coolies, types of crops grown (commercial or non-commercial crops), land - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB holdings of farmers, source of water to the crops for cultivation and its supply, etc.
21.

It appears, KSLSA after study in this regard and in consultation with top level officers of few Insurance Companies Advocate, Judges etc., prepared chart of "notional income" belonging to 3 region/Zones, Bengaluru, Dharwad and Kalaburagi.

The said chart is ordinarily followed while assessment of income of victim of an accident, while settlement of Motor Vehicle Compensation claim petitions in Lok-Adalaths/Judicial disposal of such cases by MACTs, including this court.
22. In some of the cases, wages of different class of labourers may be more than the wages fixed under Workmen Compensation Act.
In the chart prepared by KSLSA, wages are not assessed on the basis of different class of labours, such as skilled, semi-skilled and unskilled.
But such division is made under Workmen Compensation Act and their minimum wages are stated in the schedule.

Since it is benevolent legislation, as stated above, notional - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB income of victim of an accident may be assessed either on the basis of chart prepared by KSLSA or Schedule of Workmen Compensation Act or on the basis of materials placed on record by the victim in the given case, whichever is beneficial to claimants.

Main goal of Tribunal or the Court is to award just and reasonable compensation to claimants/victims of an Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
5 accident and it should not be bonanza.
23. In this case, notional income of claimant as per chart prepared by KSLSA, is beneficial to claimant and hence it was accepted by the Tribunal.
It is not necessary to reduce the income on the ground that notional income stated in the schedule of wages under Workmen Compensation Act is less.
Hence, income of claimant is accepted as Rs.14,000/- per month.
24. It is an admitted fact that claimant was aged about 50 years at the time of accident.
Hence multiplier applicable is '13'.
The appellant has contended that he has been suffering from paraplegia and he is bed ridden.
He cannot move out of the bed and has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100%.

The Tribunal, on the basis of appreciating the pleadings and evidence available on record, accepted the said contention of the claimant and held that claimant is suffering from permanent disability of 100%.
Said findings are not challenged by respondents and hence it does not call for any interference.
25. The submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that Tribunal has not considered future prospects of claimant;
The said submission is tenable since claimant has been suffering from permanent disability of 100%.
Age of claimant was about 50 years as on the date of the accident.

The learned advocate for appellant submits that as held in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra),
the Tribunal ought to have added 25 to 30% of his income towards future prospects.
This fact is seriously disputed by the learned Advocate for Respondent No.2.

According to submission of learned counsel for Respondent No.2,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB claimant was aged 50 years at the time of accident.

Therefore, as per the law laid down in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra), between the age group of 50 to 60,
the addition shall be at the rate of 10% and not 25 to 30% as submitted by learned Advocate for appellant.
26. Let us consider the said point.
Undisputedly, in this case, no proof of date of birth or age has been produced by the claimant before the Tribunal.
The Tribunal, on the basis of age mentioned in the medical records as well as mentioned in the petition and his evidence, has accepted, the age of the claimant as 50 years.
Even in the medical records, date of birth of claimant is not mentioned.
Therefore, whatever age mentioned by the doctor in the medical records might be approximate age of the claimant as informed by him.
Claimant appears to be illiterate/semi-literate and a rustic villager.
He might not be knowing his exact date of birth.

Under these circumstances, it is very difficult to accept - 14 - Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB that he had completed the age of 50 years as on the date of the accident.
Even if his age was few months more than 50 years, then also it shall be considered as 50 years, till he attains the age of 51 years.

27. The learned Advocate for the appellant has relied on the followed judgments:
(a) In the case of SHASHIKALA AND OTHERS Vs. GANGALAKSHMAMMA AND ANOTHER2, rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

entities.text: SHASHIKALA AND OTHERS Vs. GANGALAKSHMAMMA AND ANOTHER2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Para No.16, their Lordships have held as under:
"Insofar as appropriate multiplier, the date of birth of the deceased as per driving license was 16- 6-1961.
On the date of accident, i.e., 14-12-2006, the deceased was aged 45 years, 5 months and 28 days, and the Tribunal has taken the age as 46 years.

Since the deceased has completed only 45 years, the High Court has rightly taken the age of the deceased as 45 years and adopted multiplier of (2015) 9 SCC 150 - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB 14 which is the appropriate multiplier and the same is maintained".
b) In the case of M.H.UMA MAHESHWARI AND OTHERS Vs. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED3, it is held as under:
"The Tribunal, by recording a finding that the deceased was in the age group of 40 to 50 years, applied the multiplier of 13 while calculating the compensation.

entities.text: M.H.UMA MAHESHWARI AND OTHERS Vs. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court, curiously while maintaining the multiplier of 13 as per the judgment of this Court in the case of Sarla Verma1, has reduced the compensation only on the ground that the deceased was aged 50 years 3 months on the date of the accident, as such the compensation is to be calculated on account of loss of dependency by granting future prospects at 15% but not 30%.
So far as the application of multiplier of 13 by the Tribunal is concerned, the High Court has not interfered with the same.
When the age of the deceased was considered in the group of 40 to 50 years, we are of the view that the High Court has committed error in granting only 15% towards future prospects instead of 30%.
As per the judgments AIR 2020 SC 5038 - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB of this Court primarily the age group is to be considered.

Considering the age group as 40 to 50 years, when the multiplier of 13 is maintained by the High Court, there is no reason or justification for reducing the compensation by granting 15% towards future prospects.

Though the learned counsel appearing for respondent no.1-Insurance Company has submitted that the compensation towards future prospects was awarded as per the Constitution Bench judgment of this Court Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
7 in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.2 but at the same time it is to be noticed that in the very same judgment in paragraph 59.3 while considering the grant of future prospects, this Court has specifically said that the addition should be 30% if the age of the deceased was in the age group of 40 to 50 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For application of multiplier, the High Court has also accepted the age group of the deceased between 40 and 50 years.
In that view of the matter, there is no reason for reducing the compensation by granting future prospects at 15% only.
For the above said reasons and in the absence of actual date of birth of claimant, we are not inclined to accept the contentions of learned Advocate for Respondent - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB No.2.
As per the law rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court (referred Supra), for the purpose of addition of future prospects, his age shall be considered as 50 years till commencement of age of 51 years.
28. In the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra), if the claimant/deceased had fixed income or permanent employment, then only the addition should be at 30%.
Otherwise, when a person is self-employed or he had no established income, future prospects to be added between age group of 40 to 50 years is 25% of the said income.
In this case, the claimant is admittedly an agriculture coolie and had no permanent income.
And hence 25% of his income needs to be added towards future prospects.

Multiplier applicable in this case is admittedly '13'.
29.
In this case, admittedly, claimant has been suffering from permanent disability of 100%.
Looking to the evidence of PWs-1 and 2, he has been wheelchair bound or bed-ridden.
He needs services of attendants to - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB do daily pursuits, around the clock.
It appears till his last breath, his condition may be the same.
He cannot enjoy remaining part of his life.
He is married person and lost his marital enjoyments.
He has lost all the enjoyment of normal human being.

30. The learned Advocate for claimant submits that the amount of compensation awarded under others heads such as, pain and suffering, attendant charges, conveyance charges, food and special diet, loss of future earnings, loss of amenities, future medical expenses are much lower side, which needs to be enhanced.
He submits that, along with wife of claimant, two others have been attending claimant through out the day from the date of accident till this day, and it needs to be continued till his death.
Therefore, minimum Rs.8 to 10 lakhs needs to be awarded under the head "attendant charges".
The claimant has lost several amenities, and is living like a vegetable.
Hence, the amount of compensation awarded under the head loss of amenities is very meager.

For Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
8 - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB aforesaid reasons, prayed to enhance the said amount and award just and reasonable amount of compensation.

31. The learned Advocate for the appellant has relied on the judgment rendered by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of VITTAL S DANDAPUR Vs. THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER4 and submitted that, in that case, this Court has awarded Rs.3 lakhs towards loss of amenities and Rs.8,64,000/- towards attendant charges.

entities.text: VITTAL S DANDAPUR Vs. THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Facts in that case also similar to facts of the present lose.
Therefore, same rule is applicable to facts of the present case and same amount needs to be awarded in the present case.
32. The learned Advocate for Respondent No.2 has submitted that, awarding of compensation amount depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
Mearly, some of the facts are similar, cannot be ground to MFA No.2450/2018 (MV-I) dd: 15.06.2020 - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:41715-DB award same amount of compensation.
It is not held in that case that in all the cases wherein victim of an accident is suffering from paraplegia, same amount of compensation shall be awarded.
Hence, submission of learned advocate for appellant in this regard is not acceptable.
The submission of the learned for Respondent No.2 is acceptable.
In the case of VITTAL S DANDAPUR (referred supra), claimant was aged about 23 years.
He was unmarried and there was nobody in the family to look after him.

Considering the said facts, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court held that, an attendant has to be paid Rs.4000/- per month and on that basis, awarded the compensation of Rs.8,64,000/- to the claimant.
The facts of the present case are different.
In this case, claimant is married person, he has wife and said to be looking after him and attending him.
Moreover, claimant in the present case is aged 50 years.
Therefore, same amount of compensation as awarded in the case of Vital S Dandapur (referred supra) can't be awarded.
The submission of learned advocate for respondent is tenable.
Awarding amount of compensation depends upon facts and circumstances of each case and it is not on arithmetical calculations.
As narrated by the learned advocate for respondent, facts of the present case is different from the facts of the case of Vittal Dandapur.
Hence same amount of compensation can't be awarded in this case.

34. In this case claimant has been suffering from paraplegia; He is permanently disabled by 100%;
and he is bedridden/wheel chair bound.

Nanjappa vs Chand Pasha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168012029/
9 35.
He has been attended by the attendants as well as his wife, around the clock.
He lost all kinds of pleasures of future life.
He lost marital enjoyment and family life.
Considering these facts, the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads are very less, which needs to be enhanced.

The compensation under the head loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability is:
 Income per Month Rs.14,000/-
 Add: 25% future Rs.3,500/-
 prospects  Net Income Rs.17,500/-
Rs.17,500X12X13=Rs.27,30,000/-.
37.

ORDER i) M.F.A.No.4877 of 2021 is partly allowed.
